Stanisław Jerzy Lec, the Polish poet and satirist, has a story titled "The Cannibal and the Knife and Fork" (from the collection Myśli nieuczesane, published in 1957) that goes roughly like this:
A man had gone on a journey and fell into the hands of cannibals. In the midst of that crowd, one face seemed familiar to him. He called out: "Aren't you so-and-so who came to our country once — we were classmates? Aren't you ashamed that now that you've come back to your kith and kin, you want to eat me?"
The former classmate said: "I really feel sorry for you, that you judge so hastily and think I'm like these others. I wish you could have been chopped to pieces and seen that when my own tribe eats you like savages, with their hands, I maintain my academic dignity and decorum — I put your flesh on the table, tie on a bib, light a candle, and eat you with a knife and fork."
As Obeid Zakani says, my purpose in reading this story — understand the point, my dear boy! So you're mistaken if you think Mr. Vance, as Vice President of the United States, is like Trump and the rest of that rabble, just because he said that when the firing-squad execution of that American soldier who shot his own comrades was about to be broadcast publicly, "I'm different from the rest of the officials and I won't watch in such a civilized manner — I might even let out a quiet ooh and aah."

"The issue is not only our present enemies; independent islands like you are also a danger to the empire, because they stand outside our order... if peoples maintain their independence, it is because they have power; and if we do not attack them, it is because we fear them. So by subjugating you, in addition to expanding our empire, we also increase our security; especially since you are islanders and weaker than others and should not be able to prevail over the masters of the sea."

According to this map, 1,287 of the 1,530 recorded locations were reported during the first 40 days of the war, while only 13 were recorded between April 9 and June 7; then, in June and July, another wave of attacks emerged with 226 reported locations, 138 of which were in southern Iran, in areas below the 30th parallel. Of the total 1,530 cases, 544 are classified as confirmed airstrikes, 550 as reported attacks, and 436 as explosions captured on video; however, in 1,142 cases, the perpetrator of the attack is not identified in the published data. This dataset merely offers a picture of the geographic and temporal distribution of reported cases and, on its own, cannot show the extent of human and civilian damage from any given attack.@sahandiranmehr

🔶This film is one of the most valuable documents of Iran's contemporary history. It shows the speech of the first Iranian at the first meeting of the United Nations in January 1946 in London. The speaker is the representative of the Iranian government, Seyyed Hassan Taghizadeh. Many consider Taghizadeh to be Iran's first true intellectual. He was a multifaceted figure. He went on to serve as ambassador, parliamentarian, minister, and president of the Senate. Alongside politics, he was also a distinguished scholar and thinker. During his time in the political arena, Taghizadeh influenced many intellectuals. Many, moved by his ideas, turned toward Western civilization. However, ill-wishers branded him "Westoxicated" and leveled the worst accusations against him. But he loved his homeland and was beholden to no one. More than a prominent and influential politician, he was an influential intellectual. He was the first politician to boldly undertake "self-criticism" and critique his own behavior and words: "When the matter of Atabak's nomination for premiership became the talk of the town, I used everything at my disposal—from the sting of my tongue to the poison of my pen—to bring him down before his premiership. In my speeches, I turned him into an absolute evil who was coming to tear down the constitution. I portrayed all his services as treason. I made such a demon of him that the blood of listeners younger than myself would boil, and they would lose control and resort to violent acts. I need not have issued a decree for terrorism to be held responsible for it; to the same extent that I make the atmosphere heated and radical, I bear moral responsibility for the consequences. When we turn our political opponent into a monster, we must be aware of our intellectual and moral responsibility."... "All my life I am paying the price for when Mohammad Ali Shah came through the door of reconciliation with the constitutionalists, I dug in my heels and opposed it."... "In the first period of my life, when I rose up in strife and aggression, I made mistakes, and I had the courage to admit this mistake." ... "The constitutionalists did not even shy away from uttering insults against the honor and reputation of the Shah in the newspapers, and the Shah's response was to file a complaint with the court, but not only was the Shah's complaint not addressed, other constitutionalists attempted an unsuccessful assassination of the Shah. Sixty years on from those days, I cannot hide my regret over the failure to reach understanding with Mohammad Ali Shah" (Andisheh-ye Pouya, Issue 39). P.S.: The fifth of Mehr was Taghizadeh's birthday. From the Instagram of: Mehrdad Hojjati @sahandiranmehr

A member of the Israeli delegation is writing down the names of those who walked out of Netanyahu's speech! The United Nations was founded after the Second World War. Poor humanity, after all that bloodshed, came slightly to its senses and said to itself: Surely from now on we'll settle things through dialogue and diplomacy and sitting around a table — not with bombs and cannons and tanks. In short, they wanted to make the world understand that human beings, if they are human beings, can use a tongue instead of teeth, and logic instead of "oldorm and boldorm"! Now, however, Trump the American — who all this time was showing off the free world and democracy and human rights, and whose predecessors brought down the Iron Curtain with that same bluster — conjures hell before everyone's eyes from behind the podium, saying that if they don't listen to him he can annihilate an entire nation; Netanyahu hoists the pagers like a trophy of honor and tells his critics: "Coward" — and the most interesting scene of all is this: him imagining himself as the monitor and snitch of Khan Bala, ruler and cherry switch in hand, waiting to hand over to His Excellency the list of names of those who didn't sit at the master's whipping post and left the session, so he can light the pipe of the "bad ones."
